source_map_note: Compiled input files were unchanged throughout the final runs. The map also includes documentation updated after the initial receive builds started.
scope: Private numeric TCP Client, MQTT 5.0 and 3.1.1, current release maturity developing
ordering: Accept PUBLISH atomically with persisted durable delivery, plus QoS2 receive identity before PUBREC.
QoS2 duplicate repeats PUBREC without another durable delivery.
Known PUBREL batches transition and identifier retirement before PUBCOMP. Delivery persists.
After physical Client and Writer retirement and fresh recovery/import, resumed session responds to retried PUBREL and permits reuse of retired id.
Close while a receive operation is pending suppresses its ACK but retains actual file duty and applies committed effects before Session end.
fixture: Actual TCP with literal peer bytes, one-byte ACK write chunks and model sequence recorded by peer at ACK reception.
Held final file sync during PUBLISH acceptance or identifier retirement. No ACK escapes the hold.
Real native temporary journal and separate fault-injected VFS journal. Reopen, replay and use a fresh Session and Client.
QoS0/1/2 acceptance, alias binding and empty-topic resolution, duplicate QoS2, identifier reuse, write refusal and Inbox quota refusal.
Retained delivery uses canonical full topic and has no connection alias. No duplicate delivery through volatile Inbox.
retained_attempts: Initial WSL wrapper failed to pass its shell redirection cleanly and ran no tests. The corrected direct WSL invocation produced the recorded results.
limits: No public durable Client factory or application delivery lease yet.
Outgoing PUBLISH scheduling and durable ACK mutation, other transports and authentication remain outstanding.
The private receive path serializes one storage transaction at a time per Client with a CloseTimeout commit budget and the existing native sync policy.
Static and shared qualification runs standard public package consumers. Private live driver runs in modular and single-header fixtures.
No controlled performance, physical power-loss, full four-product release or native 72-hour acceptance is claimed.
